title: fix(markup): adapt button helpers to layer 229 button types
body:
Fixes the build of #1850 (layer 229). CI there fails because `telegram/message/markup` still uses the `keyboardButton*` constructors that layer 229 removed.

Layer 229 splits buttons into two concrete types: `keyboardButton` with a `ButtonType` for reply keyboards, and `keyboardInlineButton` with an `InlineButtonType` for inline keyboards. This PR ports the helpers to that model.

## API changes

- Helper names are unchanged. Return types follow the new model:
  - `tg.KeyboardButton`: `Button`, `RequestPhone`, `RequestGeoLocation`, `RequestPoll`, `RequestPeer`, `SimpleWebView`
  - `tg.KeyboardInlineButton`: `URL`, `Callback`, `SwitchInline`, `Game`, `Buy`, `URLAuth`, `InputURLAuth`, `UserProfile`, `InputUserProfile`, `WebView`
- New generic helpers `KeyboardButton(text, tg.ButtonTypeClass, style...)` and `InlineButton(text, tg.InlineButtonTypeClass, style...)` cover any button type, including ones added later. The named helpers are built on them.
- New helpers for the new inline types: `Copy`, `Disabled`.
- New `InlineButtonRow`. `Row`/`SingleRow` take reply buttons; `InlineRow`, `InlineKeyboard` and the `Row` methods in `message` and `message/inline` take inline buttons.
- `URLAuth` and `UserProfile` were reply-keyboard buttons. Layer 229 only has inline forms, so they are inline now.
- Style options are unchanged.

Code that mixed reply and inline buttons in one row no longer compiles. The protocol no longer allows that either.

## Tests

- Split the row tests into inline and reply keyboards.
- Added encode/decode round-trip tests for both keyboard kinds.
- Extended the style tests to `Copy` and `Disabled`.

`go build ./...`, `go vet ./telegram/...` and `go test ./...` pass locally on top of #1850.

`telegram/message/audio.go` is not gofmt-clean on the #1850 branch. I left it out because it's unrelated.

## Motivation

We need layer 229 for ephemeral bot messages. On layer 228 the server sends `updateEphemeralBotCallbackQuery#9b380762`, which is only in `_schema/tdlib.tl`. gotd can't decode it and drops the whole `updates` container, so callback buttons on ephemeral messages can't be handled.

title: feat(calls): expose the selected ICE candidate pair
body:
`Conn` keeps its `*webrtc.ICETransport` unexported, so a caller cannot
tell whether a call went peer-to-peer or through a relay. There is no
other way to find out: nothing else on the connection carries it.

That distinction is worth having. Telegram hands its reflectors over as
ordinary TURN servers (see `iceServers`), so a relayed call shows a local
candidate of type `relay` and a direct one does not. A rising share of
relayed calls is the first sign that direct paths are being blocked
somewhere — a network, a NAT, a provider — and in production it surfaces
as "quality got worse lately" long before anyone can name why.

Read-only accessor over the existing transport. Returns `nil` before ICE
has settled, which callers can treat as unknown. It takes the connection
mutex to read the transport and releases it before calling into pion —
the same shape `Close` already uses for the same fields.

Six lines of behaviour; no new state, no new dependency.

---

Based directly on current `main`. `go test ./telegram/calls/...`, `go vet`
and `gofmt` clean.

Separate from #1839 on purpose: that one is three bug fixes for silent
inbound audio, this is a small API addition, and mixing them would make
both harder to judge.
